aboutH2: Valiant Recovery Kelowna: Small-Group Residential Addiction Treatment in the Okanagan
intro: Valiant Recovery Kelowna is a private residential addiction program in a large home on Lakeshore Road in Kelowna's Lower Mission. Valiant says it opened here in 2010 and still calls the Kelowna house its premier location. The same company, Valiant Recovery Inc., runs Valiant Behavioural Health near Ottawa.

The program is deliberately tiny. Valiant's site advertises a 2-client maximum and 40 private counselling sessions a month, with daily groups on top. Stays are 30, 60, 90 or 120 days, clients arrive already sober, and the fees are paid privately rather than through BC's health authorities.

pillars.title: A Private Home Near Okanagan Lake
pillars.body: Treatment happens in a 4,700 square foot house on Lakeshore Road, in the Lower Mission area of south Kelowna. Groups meet in a great room with vaulted ceilings and a two-storey marble fireplace. The house has 6 bedrooms and 7 bathrooms, and a self-contained 2 bedroom suite with its own entrance lets women sleep apart from men. There is a gym, a hot tub with 37 jets, an infrared sauna and a home theatre with a 150 inch screen used for recovery videos. Staff cook the meals, and in summer a lot of the day moves out to the backyard patio. The lake beaches and walking trails are close by.

pillars.title: Phone and Video Counselling Once You Are Home
pillars.body: Before discharge, a follow-up counsellor helps you find support groups where you live and builds an aftercare plan with you. Valiant includes 5 hours of phone or video counselling for every 30 days you stayed, or 10 hours on the Executive Program, and more can be bought. People recovering from alcohol use can sign up for Soberlink breathalyzer monitoring for extra accountability. Graduates of the 90 day program who complete their aftercare and then relapse can come back, and Valiant credits them a free month.

pillars.title: Most of the Work Happens One to One
pillars.body: Valiant puts private counselling at the centre of the program and advertises 40 one-to-one sessions a month. Daily groups cover anxiety and depression, grief and loss, anger, codependency, trauma, the 12 steps and relapse prevention. Trained counsellors run the Genesis Process, a relapse prevention course that looks at old beliefs and past trauma, and EMDR is offered for trauma. Spiritual counselling is part of the program, though recovery.com notes clients are not pressured and can choose other therapies instead. Approved family members can visit on weekends and join a free family session.

overview: Valiant Recovery Kelowna treats alcohol and drug addiction, including cocaine, opioids, methamphetamine and prescription drugs, along with behavioural addictions such as sex addiction and gambling. Its counsellors also work on the mental health problems that often come with addiction, including anxiety, depression, bipolar disorder, ADHD, OCD and trauma.

location.heading: Valiant Recovery Kelowna in Kelowna, British Columbia
location.intro: Valiant Recovery's house is at 3517 Lakeshore Road in Kelowna's Lower Mission, in the Central Okanagan, a short walk from the Okanagan Lake beaches. From Vancouver it is about 4 hours by car over the Coquihalla and Highway 97C, or about an hour's flight into Kelowna International Airport; West Kelowna is about 20 minutes away, Vernon and Penticton about an hour, and Kamloops roughly 2 hours.

faqIntro: Answers come from the centre's own website and its recovery.com profile. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: What kind of program is Valiant Recovery Kelowna?
faqs.a: It is a private residential (inpatient) addiction program run in a large house in Kelowna, British Columbia. Clients live on site for 30, 60, 90 or 120 days. Valiant says it takes a maximum of 2 clients at a time, so most of the work happens in one-to-one counselling rather than big groups.

faqs.q: How much does Valiant Recovery Kelowna cost?
faqs.a: Recovery.com lists an estimated $10,500 to $32,000 CDN per month. Valiant does not post prices on its own site and says the fee depends on the program level, the length of stay and whether detox is needed, so call admissions for an information package with pricing.

faqs.q: Is Valiant Recovery covered by BC public health care?
faqs.a: No. Valiant Recovery Inc. is a pay-for-fee service and says it is not government funded or covered by provincial health care. It accepts cheques, cash, debit, major credit cards and wire transfers, offers Medicard financing, and notes that some private insurers may pay part of the cost.

faqs.q: Does Valiant Recovery Kelowna offer detox?
faqs.a: Clients must be clean and sober before they move into the house. Valiant says it can arrange detox before treatment when it is needed, but only for people going on to its residential program. Its FAQ adds that anyone who arrives still in withdrawal is taken to a hospital or local detox centre at their own expense.

Valiant offers 30, 60, 90 and 120 day stays. The centre recommends 90 days where possible and offers a free month of treatment to anyone who relapses after finishing the 90 day program and the prescribed aftercare.

faqs.q: How much one-to-one counselling do clients get?
faqs.a: Valiant's site advertises 40 private one-to-one sessions a month, around 10 a week, on top of daily group sessions. Groups cover topics such as anxiety and depression, grief and loss, anger, codependency, trauma, the 12 steps and relapse prevention.

It is Valiant's top program level for working professionals. It includes the master suite, laptop and internet use so you can keep an eye on your business, 6 family counselling hours, 10 aftercare counselling hours, weekend outings and free pick-up and drop-off at the airport.

faqs.q: Where is Valiant Recovery Kelowna and how do I get there?
faqs.a: The house is on Lakeshore Road in Kelowna's Lower Mission area, near the Okanagan Lake beaches. From Vancouver it is about 4 hours by car over the Coquihalla and Highway 97C, or about an hour's flight into Kelowna International Airport. Kamloops is roughly 2 hours away and Vernon and Penticton about an hour.

faqs.q: Can family visit or stay in touch?
faqs.a: Yes. Approved family members can visit on weekends and Valiant offers family therapy sessions during the visit at no extra charge. Visitors stay in nearby hotels. Phone calls and emails are allowed at set times and may be monitored.

faqs.q: What support is there after I leave?
faqs.a: Valiant includes 5 hours of phone or video counselling for every 30 days of treatment, or 10 hours on the Executive Program. Before discharge a follow-up counsellor helps you set up support groups at home, and Soberlink breathalyzer monitoring is available for people recovering from alcohol use.
